title: Strict-PQ standalone transaction proof compression
decision: Reject off-block leaf proofs and block-aggregate consensus authority; require one self-contained standalone proof per canonical transaction.

rejected.reason: Does not currently have an independently reviewed strict-PQ parameter set.
Current implementation is non-ZK and tops out at a 120-bit profile.

rejected.option: Unmodified upstream IronSpartan at the historical 520-action ceiling
rejected.reason: The current SHA-256/GF(2^128)/96-bit profile is not release-qualified, and naive strict-profile field widening projects above the 1 MiB fresh-profile cap. The direct architecture remains the prototype base only with compact commitments and wide challenges.

rejected.option: Current wrapped Binius ZK per action
rejected.reason: Measured 298304 to 321120 bytes at an insufficient 96-bit/SHA-256 profile.

required_controls: Canonical byte-native statement and fixed-layout SHAKE256 relation
One unchanged standalone proof remains in every canonical transaction
Peers validate the proof before relay and miners include the same bytes
Fresh nodes validate canonical blocks without sidecars, caches, or aggregates
Concrete composed QROM calculator reports at least 128 bits
Spend secrets, note randomness, and rho each carry at least 384 bits of entropy
Maximum-shape standalone artifact is at most 1048576 bytes with a 524288-byte optimization target
Fresh rules hash and genesis; old profiles decode-only
